excerpts.authority: Demo National Electricity Regulatory Authority (DNERA) — fictional placeholder
excerpts.documentTitle: Illustrative Distributed Generation Rules for Industrial Facilities
excerpts.text: Industrial facilities may install self-consumption solar PV systems without a generation-capacity limit tied to grid export, provided the system does not export power to the distribution network. Roof-mounted systems require the facility to hold ownership of the roof, or written authorization from the property owner, before connection approval is granted by the local distribution company.

excerpts.authority: Demo National Electricity Regulatory Authority (DNERA) — fictional placeholder
excerpts.documentTitle: Illustrative Net-Metering Program Rules for Commercial and Industrial Customers
excerpts.text: Net-metering interconnection is available to commercial and industrial customers with generation capacity up to 20,000 kW per site. Systems above this threshold must apply under the separate independent-power-producer program. All net-metering systems must pass a technical interconnection study before energization, expected to take 30 to 60 business days from application. Export is credited at the volumetric net-metering rate published by the distribution company.

excerpts.documentTitle: Illustrative Environmental Screening Note for Renewable Energy Siting
excerpts.text: Proposed renewable energy sites that intersect a designated protected area require an environmental impact assessment and written clearance from the environmental authority before any construction permit may be issued.
